summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with an embedded software focus. Develops embedded control software in C on STM32 and Arduino microcontrollers - timer-triggered ADC sampling, interrupt-driven UART, a low-level I2C driver, and closed-loop feedback control at 15 kHz PWM - and sets up and troubleshoots the bench hardware it runs on.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed embedded software for a wearable gesture-recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter by troubleshooting at the bench through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback control, leading a 25-member team across PCB fabrication and software integration.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment; used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture and a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz rate, verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot - Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction on Arduino Due: derived heading from dual-axis quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR) and fed angular error back into rotation PWM, decoding quadrature from first principles as a 4-bit state machine on hardware interrupts at 15 kHz PWM.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through bench testing and systematic troubleshooting, reaching 100% pick reliability over 10/10 trials on a three-layer distributed system linked over static IP Ethernet.
